 Most recent Most popular 'Amazing club with amazing fans' published at 18:26 GMT 18:26 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds winger Noah Okafor, speaking to BBC MOTD: "The first goal came after Dom [Calvert-Lewin] gave me a perfect ball. My first touch wasn't perfect so I did a body movement and then found the corner. This is how I trained in the last few weeks. 
 "The second goal I will need to rewatch but I'm extremely happy."
 On the overall performance: "We know our qualities, we have trained a lot and it's a big compliment on the whole team. We have to keep going and working hard.
Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] had chances, normally he would score them, and I told him at half-time that he would score. We're really happy for him."
 On the Leeds fans: "The support from the fans was incredible. The support is unbelievable, it's an amazing club with amazing fans."

 'His talent is bigger than this performance' published at 18:24 GMT 18:24 GMT 
 FT: Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi to BBC Match of the Day on Luca Williams-Barentt's performance: "He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance. It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.
 "The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham's dressing room now is a good environment for him.
 "I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.
 "He's a mature guy. He is smart and understands the situation. He has great behaviour inside the group and the group is good enough to help him stay calm and to play without pressure, because he has to enjoy it on the pitch. He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."
 On team-mate Savio's injury: "I am sorry for Savio because he is a crucial player for us. I hope it's not a big problem for him."
 12 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Created history' published at 18:23 GMT 18:23 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds manager Daniel Farke, speaking to BBC MOTD: "The last time this club was able to win here was last century. We have created history but it doesn't feel like this. We fully deserved to win this game and it's great for everyone connected with Leeds."
 On the tactics: "We came here to win the game. We spoke the whole week about this and wanted to make this our game where we play on the front foot. We didn't want to allow Chelsea to control the mood. 
 "We need to have good fitness levels and I have smart players who understand how we want to press and play. We have to be more concentrated to execute what we want to do. Desire is second to none and we are competitive in the best league in the world."
 On Noah Okafor: "We missed him a lot and also Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] had a tough period but they are both key players. I was overthinking whether to start Noah after a long time out but it was the right decision. He was key today."

 'Fragile moment' published at 18:20 GMT 18:20 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, speaking to BBC MOTD: "We are disappointed and sad. It was tough to deal with the defeat and we're in a fragile moment. 
 "We have lost a bit of the confidence which we were playing with. It's a delicate moment but we have to go through it together and find solutions. 
 "The first half an hour was good but we conceded the equaliser and weren't too comfortable and lost some momentum. 
We could have done more in the second half but we didn't regain the confidence to have a real go and couldn't push hard enough to score one goal, which would have changed the momentum."
 On what is biggest issue at the moment: "Everything is related. It's the confidence, this fragility at the moment, the demand of the game, the physicality - everything is related."

 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Before Saturday, Leeds' most recent win at Stamford Bridge was in December 1999 - when a 2-0 victory took them top of the Premier League
 By Bobbie Jackson BBC Sport journalist Noah Okafor scored twice to deliver Leeds' first win at Chelsea since 1999 and propel the visitors up to sixth in the Premier League. 
 Chelsea, looking to bounce back from defeat at Sunderland, struck first through Emmanuel Emegha on his full debut.
 The Netherlands forward, who joined in the summer, scored his first goal for the club in the 28th minute, lashing home a left-footed strike.
 But Okafor levelled three minutes later, taking advantage of the Blues' scrambling backline to slide into the far corner.
 Dominic Calvert-Lewin spurned several chances to register in the first half - hitting the crossbar and having two headers saved - but made no mistake from the penalty spot early in the second half.
 Referee Michael Oliver awarded the spot-kick when Morgan Rogers was deemed to have used his arm to block Jayden Bogle's attempt at goal, and Calvert-Lewin confidently found the bottom corner.
 Leeds were in full control in the 58th minute when Okafor hooked a bobbling ball into the roof of the net.
 Xabi Alonso swiftly made a double change, bringing on Danny Welbeck and Pedro Neto, but Chelsea's woes in front of goal continued as Leeds held firm.
 Brenden Aaronson put the icing on the cake for Leeds deep into stoppage time, breaking clear from the halfway line and slotting into the bottom corner.
 Chelsea slip to eighth in the league with Leeds climbing to sixth, just a point shy of fourth-placed Bournemouth.
 Have your say on Chelsea's performance 
 What did you make of Leeds' display? 
 Chelsea analysis: Pressure building on Alonso 
 Figure caption, Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United
 Chelsea's attack was firing at the start of the season, with 15 goals in their first six games, but the Blues have struggled to maintain that threat.
 The absence of joint-top scorer Joao Pedro is clearly being felt and Alonso has spent the past few weeks trying to find a solution.
 Welbeck, Neto and Morgan Rogers have all been deployed through the middle - with little success as Chelsea had failed to score in three of their past four across all competitions - but Emegha offered hope their fortunes could be about to turn.
 Injuries have restricted the 23-year-old's game time this term, but he marked his first league start with a fine strike to break the deadlock.
 But he was unable to impose himself further on the game as Chelsea found it difficult to work beyond Leeds' high press during a competitive first half.
 After losing just one of their opening six games across all competitions under Alonso, Chelsea have now lost five of their past eight.
 Boos could be heard from some Chelsea fans in the latter stages, suggesting patience is already starting to wear thin with the Spanish boss who only took charge in the summer.
 Leeds analysis: Whites dreaming of Europe 
 Figure caption, Daniel Farke post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United
 The last time Leeds won at Stamford Bridge in December 1999, they moved above Manchester United to top the Premier League standings.
 Although there is no talk of title contention - at this stage - Leeds are quietly building momentum and on the fringes of a European place.
 Their strong start to the season has been built largely on the foundations of a strong defensive line - only Arsenal and Brighton have conceded fewer than their tally of nine.
 Leeds experienced just how prolific Chelsea could be earlier this season when losing 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in the Carabao Cup, but had clearly learned a lesson and kept the Blues at bay.
 Calvert-Lewin led the line as an archetypal number nine should, bullying Chelsea's defenders and bringing his team-mates into play.
 The England striker got his reward from the penalty spot after earlier chances went begging, but Okafor was the star of the show.
 The Switzerland forward showcased different qualities for each of his strikes - wriggling beyond defenders for his first and emphatically smashing home his second.
